title: Release Notes (Draft): Product & Docs updates supporting the Latency/$ Benchmark Report
author: Wei Chen
body:
## Summary
This draft release note captures small product and documentation updates shipping alongside the public-facing Latency/$ Benchmark Report. These changes are intentionally lightweight and focused on: (1) making regional/model selection explicit, (2) aligning Console screenshots and terminology with how results are presented, and (3) providing a safe, reproducible path for customers who want to validate results against their own workloads.

## Who this is for
- Developers using Redwood Hosted API (OpenAI-compatible + native SDKs) who need clarity on region selection and reproducibility.
- Solutions Engineering / Sales engineers who will reference Console views and region language during benchmark-related conversations.
- Security-conscious prospects who ask how the benchmark was run without exposing customer data.

## Customer impact (TL;DR)
- No breaking API changes.
- Minor documentation clarifications for region selection and request headers.
- Console screenshots and UI labels updated to match how the benchmark report explains latency percentiles, throughput, and unit cost.
- New optional docs/examples to help users reproduce a scaled-down version of the benchmark methodology.

---

## 1) Region selection documentation clarified (Hosted API + OpenAI-compatible)
### What changed
We clarified how to explicitly target a region for inference requests and how region routing behaves when a region is not specified.

### Why
The benchmark report presents results per region. Prospects and customers need to know exactly how to send traffic to a specific region (and how to confirm where a request landed) to reproduce comparable measurements.

### Documentation updates
- Added a dedicated section: "Selecting a region" with:
  - Supported region identifiers used in docs and examples
  - Request header(s) for OpenAI-compatible traffic
  - SDK configuration snippets for explicit region pinning
  - Notes on default routing behavior (when region is omitted)

### Notes / constraints
- We do not claim that any single region is universally fastest; results are presented per-region and subject to workload shape and variance.
- Customers running Dedicated/Private should validate region behavior against their deployment mode (hosted routing policies do not necessarily apply).

### References
- redwood-openai-compat PR: pr-318-region-header-doc-clarification

---

## 2) Region availability notes updated (NA/EU + APAC coverage)
### What changed
Updated region availability pages and footnotes to align with the report’s coverage table and the exact region names used in the benchmark.

### Why
During internal review, we saw confusion caused by mismatched naming across:
- docs region list
- Console region dropdown labels
- benchmark report tables

### Documentation updates
- Normalized region naming conventions (e.g., "us-east" vs "US East") and added a short mapping table.
- Added a short callout explaining that latency may vary by:
  - time of day
  - network path
  - request concurrency / token mix

---

## 3) Console screenshots and metric labels aligned to benchmark terminology
### What changed
We updated Console UI labels and screenshots used in the report to match the definitions in the methodology appendix.

### Details
- Standardized percentile labeling across relevant charts: "p50 latency" and "p95 latency" (instead of mixed "median" / "p95").
- Clarified throughput units in relevant views (requests/s vs tokens/s) where applicable.
- Added a small tooltip/link-out in the latency chart view for: "How latency percentiles are computed" (docs link).

### Why
The benchmark report emphasizes methodology. UI labels and report terminology must match to avoid “metric mismatch” objections.

### Notes
- This is a presentation/clarity improvement. No changes to underlying latency computation.

---

## 4) Benchmark reproducibility materials (docs + example)
### What changed
Added a minimal reproducibility guide and example so customers can run a smaller-scale version of the benchmark methodology against:
- their prompt shapes
- their target regions
- their expected concurrency

### Why
A consistent “how to reproduce” story is part of credibility. We want customers to validate the results without requiring access to internal tooling or sensitive telemetry.

### What’s included
- A step-by-step reproduction guide that:
  1) pins model and region
  2) disables accidental local caching artifacts
  3) uses a defined warmup window
  4) runs multiple trials and reports variance
  5) compares results using p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens (where available)

### References
- redwood-examples PR: pr-211-reproduce-benchmark-example

---

## 5) Quickstart link + UTM hygiene (Docs / SDK)
### What changed
Added a single, non-intrusive reference to the benchmark report in the Python SDK quickstart and docs navigation (UTM-tagged).

### Why
The report is a top-of-funnel asset. We want attribution that doesn’t degrade developer experience.

### Notes
- Link placement is intentionally minimal and does not block the quickstart.
- UTM parameters are managed by Marketing Ops.

### References
- redwood-sdk-python PR: pr-733-utm-and-report-link-in-quickstart

---

## 6) Benchmark tables publishing reliability (Docs hosting notes)
### What changed
Added internal documentation notes for serving the public benchmark tables reliably (CDN caching, versioning, rollback).

### Why
During launch week we expect traffic spikes and frequent linking from social/press.

### Notes
- Public tables are a sanitized subset (no per-request logs; no customer-identifying traces).
- We version benchmark datasets and label the report with the dataset version.

---

## Known limitations and disclaimers (must remain in externally-facing pages)
These points are required by our public benchmarking claims guidelines and must remain in the landing page, appendix, and any derivative content:
- Results are workload-dependent; the report reflects defined workloads, distributions, and settings.
- Regional results are not globally comparable without considering network and concurrency.
- We report variance/run-to-run stability and do not imply “always fastest” claims.
- No customer data is used; no customer telemetry is disclosed.

---

## Approval checklist (before publish)
- [ ] Methodology terms match the report appendix and internal methodology page.
- [ ] Region names and identifiers match Console and SDK docs.
- [ ] Console screenshots are current (captured within the final benchmark window) and do not contain customer identifiers.
- [ ] Marketing UTM parameters are correct and tested.
- [ ] Legal review completed for any externally visible wording changes.
